messages:
incident-bot: CRITICAL - Elevated 5xx rate observed from control-plane dependencies (auth/org-lookup/billing). Rule: controlplane.dependency_errors > 1.5% for 3m. Links: https://ops.redwood.example.com/alerts/ctrl-deps-5xx
Ravi: oncall SRE here, ack'ing the page. Beginning triage. Can someone confirm recent deploys to org-lookup or gateway?
Sam: auth had a small rollout ~10m ago (rev a3c4). No failure flagged on deploy. Gateway had a config push 8m ago to adjust timeouts.
Nina: org-lookup metrics: request latency p50=120ms -> now p50=600ms, p99 > 2s, queue length jumped. Seeing increased DB wait times.
Jules: support queue: multiple customers reporting login failures and webhook retries. Marked 3 customers as P1. Notifying accounts.
Ravi: quick smoke - hitting gateway endpoint gives 504 intermittently from our London edge:
```
$ http --timeout 10 GET https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/auth/token
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
{"error":"upstream timeout"}
```
Ravi: hypothesis: org-lookup slow -> auth blocks -> gateway timeouts -> client retries -> cascade.
Sam: confirm: auth is synchronous on org-lookup for token requests to fetch org settings. If org-lookup stalls, auth blocks threads.
Ravi: mitigation options, in order of speed/impact:
- enable gateway circuit-breaker for org-lookup (fail fast)
- flip auth to use cached org data for reads (stale-ok) for 15m
- scale org-lookup horizontally
- apply DB query optimizations (longer term)
Which should we do now?
Nina: I'll spin up additional org-lookup pods. Sam, can you enable cached reads? Might be a config flag `ORG_LOOKUP_CACHE_ALLOW_STALE=true`.
Sam: can do a config toggle for auth to accept stale org metadata for token issuance for known customers. That reduces dependency.
Ravi: Ken? (not here) - whoever owns gateway, can we set CB? (cc @deploy-bot)
deploy-bot: rolling config change request queued: /deploy/config/gateway/circuit-breakers
Ravi: ok start with circuit-breaker + stale cache + scale. Nina start scale. Sam flip cache flag. I'll watch SLOs and error rates.
Nina: scaling now: `kubectl scale deployment/org-lookup --replicas=8` (was 4) -> created 4 new pods. Est. 2-4m to warm up.
Sam: flipping cached read flag in auth config:
```
PATCH /config/service/auth
{"org_lookup_stale_ok":"true","org_cache_ttl":"900s"}
# response: 200
```
Sam: enabled. Routing reads to cache when DB latency high.
Ravi: enabling gateway circuit-breaker to short-circuit after 3s and fail-open for non-blocking routes.
```
PATCH /config/service/gateway
{"cb_org_lookup_threshold_ms":3000, "cb_fail_open":true}
# 200 OK
```
Ravi: monitoring...
(90s)
Ravi: error rate decreased but still elevated: overall 5xx from 2.4% -> 0.8%. Auth 5xx <1%. p95 latency improving. Good trend.
Jules: sent customers an update: "We've applied mitigations to reduce auth failures. Monitoring and will follow up."
Nina: new pods are up and passing readiness. Connection queue depth dropping. DB waits still visible but reduced.
Sam: tracing shows many org-lookup calls have DB statements waiting on a table scan. Likely missing index on org_settings.lookup_key under high concurrency.
Ravi: create follow-ups: ENGR-4603 - investigate DB index and query plan; ENGR-4604 - consider caching layer for org metadata; ENGR-4605 - improve circuit-breaker default thresholds.
PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Ravi. Priority P1. Escalation if errors >1% for 30m.
Ravi: handoff plan: I'll stay 20m to verify stability then hand to Nina for deep-dive. Reduce paging threshold to 0.8% for next 60m.
Nina: taking follow-up. My deep-dive ETA 60-90m. Will coordinate with DB team.
Sam: artifact links: traces: https://traces.redwood.example.com/trace/ef12ab, logs archived: s3://incidents/1800123456/ , gateway snapshot saved.
Jules: scheduling customer follow-ups at +30m and +3h. Notifying account teams for P1s.
Ravi: incident moved to mitigation and monitoring. Marking initial impact window 22:40 - ongoing, but mitigated for most customers. Leaving this thread to Nina for root cause. Thanks team :thumbsup:
